function: Configures RIS phase shifts: a ViT maps a desired channel-impulse-response image, built from user positions, to the phases of the N RIS elements (p. 6)
system: BS with P linear antennas, single-antenna users (P x 1 channels), passive reflecting RIS with N=100 elements, BS-user link blocked; carrier frequency not stated (p. 3, 4, 5)
method: Supervised vision transformer (patch embedding, transformer encoder, MLP) trained with MSE on RIS-phase labels from a closed form (one user) and an unsupervised DNN (multi-user) (p. 4-7)
data_channel: Own geometry-based stochastic RIS channel (Ricean K-factor, 3GPP path gain only); 25000 simulated CIR images per case of 1, 2, 3 users; no measured data (p. 4-5)
test_conditions: Trained on 1-3 users, N=100 RIS elements (p. 5); tested on Gaussian-Markov trajectories and 3-10 initial users with the same trained networks (p. 8, 14)
baselines: Classical: projected gradient ascent, coordinate descent, zero phase, random phase; learned: CNN and fully connected DNN on the same input (p. 10-11)
metrics: Weighted RMSE of regenerated versus desired CIR image, coverage probability, CIR magnitude, LCR, AFD, received power, SINR (p. 9-14)
q1_support: p. 4: "distance-dependent model by 3GPP standardized channel model [37], [38]" applies only to the path gains; clusters, K-factor and scatterers follow the authors' own geometry-based model (Eqs. 3-8). No CDL/TDL, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 14: "the trained networks, including ViT, CNN, and DNN are utilized to predict RIS phase under different initial user numbers"; Fig. 17 spans 3-10 users, while training used p. 5: "single user, two users, and three users".
q3_support: p. 11: "solution effect based on ViT network performs best among all compared methods"; compared are CNN and DNN (learned, p. 10-11) and PGA, CD, zero and random phase (classical, p. 11), on weighted RMSE (Fig. 10) and coverage probability (Fig. 12).
q4_support: p. 12: "imposes significant computational overhead" is a qualitative remark on CD and PGA; no FLOPs, parameter count, complexity order or runtime of the ViT is reported.
q5_support: p. 5: "each scenario contains 25000 images" produced by the authors' own simulator; no code or data link, no public dataset and no measurements.
notes: Published version, IEEE TWC 2026, pp. 647-663. Area 3: the ViT outputs the N RIS phases from a desired CIR image. Its labels come from a closed form (one user) and an unsupervised DNN (several users), so they are not optimal targets. q2 rests on the axis of Fig. 17 (3-10 users, p. 14) against training with 1-3 users (p. 5); the user counts are read from the figure, not from running text. q1 is 0 because only the path gain is taken from 3GPP TR 38.901 [37].
